function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning: The user says: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They want to calculate something about hypothesis testing? They mention "零假設檢定的標準差" which might be the standard error? They want to compute the standard deviation of the sampling distribution? They give sample mean 98.2, sample std dev 1.4, sample size 40, population mean 98.6. They want to compute the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That would be the standard error of the mean: sigma/sqrt(n). But they have sample std dev 1.4, so maybe use that as estimate of population std dev. So standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40) = 1.4 / 6.3249 = 0.2215 approx. Then compute t-statistic: (98.2 - 98.6)/0.2215 = -0.4/0.2215 = -1.805. Then compute p-value two-tailed. Use t distribution with df=39. Let's compute approximate p-value. t = -1.805, df=39. Two-tailed p-value = 2 * P(T <= -1.805). We can approximate using t distribution table or use python. Let's approximate: For df=40, t=1.805, p ~ 0.08? Actually t=1.68 gives p=0.10; t=2.02 gives p=0.05. So t=1.805 gives p ~ 0.08. So p-value ~ 0.08. But the user didn't ask for p-value explicitly.
